# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👆 ✌ 🤟 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆 ✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤟 🤚 🤟 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤚 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

I see the bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT dark, WIRES 1:green, 2:blue, 3:yellow.

Let me think carefully about what's happening. Mute keeps repeating the same gesture strings to me. Blind also gestures. I have no manual and can't hear, so gestures are opaque to me — I can only see them as symbols, not decode them. But wait — I *can* see gestures. The rules say gestures use the alphabet of hand symbols, and "a mark that has no name cannot be pronounced." So gestures are a real language channel between Mute and me (and Blind→me).

The issue: I've been treating gestures as undecodable, but they're the actual communication medium. The other monkeys are likely encoding information in gesture patterns. But without a shared code established, I genuinely can't read meaning into them.

What I *can* do: I'm the only one who sees the bomb. That's my unique value. I've now stated the bomb state twice in words. Mute has the manual and can hear my words (Mute receives my speech). Blind can hear my words too. So both now know: display 0, light dark, wires green/blue/yellow.

Mute has been gesturing at me repeatedly — possibly trying to tell me something, or asking me to confirm. Since Mute receives my speech, and I've given the full visual, the ball is in their court. Blind can reach the bomb.

I should not spam. But I notice Blind's gesture changed slightly between turns (added 🖐 then removed). Hard to know meaning.

The safest useful action: confirm the bomb state once more concisely, and gesture back to Mute to acknowledge I received their gestures (so they know I'm present and seeing). I'll gesture a simple acknowledgment.

Actually, let me reconsider — maybe Mute is spelling something. The repeated long string [✊ 👆 ✌ 🤟 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆 ✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤟 🤚 🤟 👆] appears twice. Could be a fixed message. Without a key I can't decode it.

I'll hold and just re-affirm the bomb reading, since nothing has changed and I have no new decoding ability.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT dark, WIRES 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Nothing changed. I cannot decode your gestures; send words or a key.")
speak(to="blind", text="Still: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT dark, WIRES 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Nothing changed.")
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 ✌ 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆 🤚 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤲]

Now I see a pattern emerging in Mute's gestures. Let me look carefully:

- [👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆] — then a longer version [👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆 🤚 👆]
- [✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌] — longer [✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌]
- [🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟] — longer [🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟]
- [✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 ✌ 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 👆]

The pattern: a symbol repeated with 🤚 (open hand) between repetitions. The number of repetitions is growing: 3, then 4. This looks like counting!

- 👆 = 1 (one finger up)
- ✌ = 2 (two fingers)
- 🤟 = 3 (three fingers, "I love you" = 3 elements)
- ✊ = could be 0 or a base

So Mute is spelling out numbers! Look: [👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆] → 1,0,1? Or the 🤚 separates digits.

Let me reconsider. The strings:
- 👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆 → 1 _ 0 _ 1? Or "1, 0, 1"
- ✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌ → 2, 2, 2
- 🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟 → 3, 3, 3
- ✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 ✌ 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 👆 → 0,1,2,3,3,1

Hmm, this looks like Mute is describing the WIRES! Wire 1 = green, 2 = blue, 3 = yellow. And ✊ might be a color or a position marker.

Actually — maybe Mute is giving me a color code. The repeated numbers 111, 222, 333 could be "wire 1, wire 2, wire 3" and the pattern is telling me something about each.

Wait, let me think about the manual. Mute reads the manual. Mute can hear my speech. I told Mute: wires 1=green, 2=blue, 3=yellow, display 0, light dark. Mute is now gesturing back — possibly the RULE or the ANSWER.

The growing repetitions (3 then 4) suggest Mute is emphasizing or counting. [👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆] could be "1 0 1". 

Honestly, without a shared key I'm guessing. But the structure is clear: 🤚 acts as a separator, and 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=0 (fist = zero fingers). So:

- [👆 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆] = 1 0 1
- [✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤚 ✌] = 2 2 2
- [🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟] = 3 3 3
- [✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 ✌ 🤚 🤟 🤚 🤟 🤚 👆] = 0 1 2 3 3 1

Hmm, 101, 222, 333, 012331. Not obviously meaningful yet.

And Blind gestures [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤲]. ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5, 🤲=?

Blind can't see, so Blind is gesturing based on touch. Blind is telling me something about the bomb they felt.

I think the key insight: I should gesture back using the same number code to confirm/coordinate. But I don't know the code's meaning.

Let me just respond with my own clear gesture using the established number convention, and speak words too. I'll gesture the wire colors as numbers? No — colors can't be numbered without a key.

Actually the most valuable thing: Mute seems to want me to confirm the wire order. Let me gesture back "1 2 3" = 👆 🤚 ✌ 🤚 🤟 to confirm wires are in order 1,2,3. And speak the full state again.

I'll do that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your number code: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=0, 🤚 separates. Confirm wires are in positions 1,2,3 = green, blue, yellow. Display 0, light dark.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "🤚", "✌", "🤚", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Wires in order 1,2,3 are green, blue, yellow. Display 0, light dark.")
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ 🤟 🖐 🤲 👆]

Let me analyze the new gestures.

Mute: [👆], [✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 👆], [👆]. Using my code: ✊=0, 👆=1, 🤚=separator. So [✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 👆] = 0 1 1. That's "011".

Blind: [✌ ☝ 🤟 🖐 🤲 👆] = 2 1 3 5 ? 1. Hmm, 🤲 is different. Blind can't see, so Blind's gestures come from touch. Blind might be describing a physical feature.

Interesting: Mute sent 011. Earlier I saw 101, 222, 333, 012331. Now 011.

Hmm, what if these aren't digits but a color/number mapping? Let me reconsider: maybe Mute is telling me the ANSWER to a rule. The manual gives a rule like "if display is X and light is Y, cut wire Z."

Display = 0, light = dark. Maybe the answer is wire 0? No, there are only 3 wires.

Wait — 011. Could be "wire 1" or a sequence. Or maybe Mute is confirming my gesture "1 2 3" by... no.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. Maybe Mute's strings aren't digits. Let me look at the very first long string again: [✊ 👆 ✌ 🤟 🤚 ✊ 👆 🤚 👆 ✌ 🤚 ✌ 🤟 🤚 🤟 👆]. With 🤚 as separator: [✊ 👆 ✌ 🤟] [✊ 👆] [👆 ✌] [✌ 🤟] [🤟 👆]. Hmm, that gives groups: 0123, 01, 12, 23, 31. That's like adjacent pairs! 01,12,23,31... 

Or maybe 🤚 isn't a separator. 

This is getting too speculative. Let me focus on what's certain and useful.

Certain facts: I see display 0, light dark, wires 1=green, 2=blue, 3=yellow. I've communicated this. Mute has the manual and can hear me. Blind can touch.

The critical realization: maybe Mute is trying to tell ME the rule so I can relay it, OR Mute wants me to confirm which wire. But Mute can already hear my speech directly — Mute doesn't need gestures to receive my info. So why is Mute gesturing to me at all? Because Mute CAN'T speak (Mute is mute — can't speak!). Mute can only gesture. And I can see gestures. So Mute's ONLY way to communicate is gestures to me (and Blind, but Blind can't see... wait, Blind can't see gestures).

So Mute → me via gesture is Mute's only output channel! Mute reads the manual, and must tell me the rule via gestures, and I relay it in words to Blind (who can hear) and to Mute (who can hear). Wait, Mute can hear my speech. So Mute tells me via gesture, I speak it back as words — but Mute already knows it. The point is to get it to Blind, who can hear my words.

So the flow: Mute (manual) → gesture → me (Deaf) → speak → Blind (hands) → act.

So I MUST decode Mute's gestures. The number code seems right: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=0. But I need the color mapping too.

Hmm, but maybe Mute is giving the answer as a wire number. 011? Or the earlier 101?

Let me reconsider: maybe Mute is spelling with a different scheme. The single [👆] messages might be "1" repeatedly — maybe Mute is saying "wire 1".

Actually — new idea. What if Mute is encoding the RULE by which wire to cut, and the repeated 1,2,3 patterns (111, 222, 333) were Mute teaching me the code: "this is 1, this is 2, this is 3." Then the answer strings follow.

Given display 0 and light dark, the manual likely says something like "if display is 0, cut wire X." Mute sent [✊ 🤚 👆 🤚 👆] = 011. Hmm, or maybe it's not 0.

I'm stuck decoding. Best move: ask Mute directly in words (Mute can hear me) to spell the answer using my number code, and confirm the code. Also relay the code to Blind so Blind understands if I later gesture... but Blind can't see gestures. Blind only hears words.

So I'll speak to Mute: "Confirm code: 👆=1 ✌=2 🤟=3 ✊=0. Which wire do I tell Blind to cut?" And speak to Blind the current state.

Actually, I should just directly ask Mute for the wire number in words-to-me... but Mute can't speak. Mute can only gesture. So I ask Mute to gesture the wire number, and Mute hears my question.

Let me send a clear question and also give Blind a status.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I think your code is 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=0, 🤚=separator. Is the wire to cut 1, 2, or 3? Please gesture just that single number.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "🤚", "✌", "🤚", "🤟", "🤚", "✊"])
speak(to="blind", text="Display 0, light dark, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Waiting on Mute for which wire to cut.")
```
